Waiting, the record, were you there — mockup v1

Three ideas from the product session. Pages are the real site and the real organiser page; 12 people is an example number — on the real page it is the count from the "tell me when it's back" sign-ups. The dashed outline marks what's new.

Scroll sideways. The phones scroll too.

1 · People waiting — for organisers

Live todayOrganiser page, live todayA market with no date tells its organiser "No upcoming date on your page yet. Add one below." Nothing says why it matters.
ProposedOrganiser page, proposedThe same card says how many people are waiting — and nothing else. Shown from the first person; the count is never invented.
ProposedThe letter, proposedOne sentence before the button, only when people are waiting. It goes in the welcome letter now and the annual "what are your dates" letter in November.

Flohmarkt am See Wollishofen on fynda.market — your page
From: fynda.market

ProposedMarket page, proposedPublic, on the claim card: an organiser looking their own market up sees people are waiting. Shown from 3 people up.

2 · The record — earlier dates

ProposedNo date: what it had this yearUnder "No next date yet", the dates it had this year, newest first. It shows the market is real and regular.
ProposedA weekly market: one line, then the listUnder the coming dates: "21 Saturdays since 2 May, none cancelled", three dates, and the rest behind a button. A date someone confirmed with "Yes, it was on" says Seen on.

3 · Were you there? — the day after

ProposedBürkliplatz, the morning afterFor two days after a date, one question under the buttons. On the day itself it appears once the market has closed.
ProposedAfter a tapOne line, and nothing else asked. "No" goes to us like a report; "Yes" marks the date as seen.
